name: Good Games
oneLine: Busman's Holiday, Cavalier, Happy To Help, Homely Sage, and They'll Be Glad They Knew Me keep a game's structure but aim the payoff at someone besides the player.
whatYouDid: You asked Mrs. Oyelaran what made her open-door tutoring a Good game rather than a Rescuer trap, and found the answer: nobody, including her, ends up worse off, and there's no Switch waiting to flip it.
confusion: The word "game" makes people assume every instance must be harmful or manipulative; Berne's own point was closer to the opposite - the structure can be reused for something closer to generosity, as long as the switch-and-payoff benefits someone other than the player, or costs no one anything real.

expand.definition: A Good game still runs an ulterior transaction and still ends in something like a payoff - the difference is who the payoff is for. Homely Sage dispenses wisdom nobody has to take; Happy To Help genuinely leaves people better off; They'll Be Glad They Knew Me structures a whole career around being remembered well.
expand.otherFraming: Not every helping pattern that looks selfless is automatically a Good game - the test is the same one that spots any game: is there a Switch waiting, and who actually ends up worse off when it comes.
expand.tryThisToday: Think of one habit of yours that structurally resembles a game - it repeats, it has an ulterior layer, it ends in some kind of payoff - and ask honestly whether anyone ends up worse off. If not, you may already be playing a Good one.
